title: fix(sdk): handle browser auth failures
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Fix browser storage and navigation errors that can crash the auth provider or leave login stuck.
- Restore saved keys without a startup request. Keep login usable when saving a new key fails; document the storage and logout limitations.
- Keep existing OAuth + PKCE and account-hook error handling. No startup checks or automatic retries.
- Simplify auth docs and comments. Add SDK tests to CI; 92 tests pass, including shuffled order, plus type-check, build and formatting. Related #12320.

gist.headline: Login keeps buzzing
gist.blurb: Browser storage occasionally has opinions. The SDK now keeps saved keys and login flows usable when storage or navigation refuses to cooperate.
gist.summary: Hardened the React SDK auth provider against browser storage and navigation failures: saved keys now restore without a startup request, and a failed key save no longer leaves login stuck, while existing OAuth + PKCE handling remains intact.
gist.impact: Browser-based SDK apps gain more reliable login recovery, with previously saved keys available immediately and new-key login still usable even when local storage cannot save it.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the React SDK authentication flow as a cozy garden gate beside a retro browser terminal: a saved key is safely tucked into a small seed vault while a few harmless storage-error pixels bounce away. Polli, wearing a tiny locksmith tool belt, keeps the gate open for a user-shaped glow; the monitor robot can hold an OAuth + PKCE map, with code-plants and flowers showing that the login path continues growing despite a fussy browser.
